item.title: AI agent vs agentic AI: the difference in plain words
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: An AI agent does one specific task on its own: sort a ticket, check an invoice, answer a set question. It acts when told to and does not plan ahead. Agentic AI starts from a goal, breaks it into steps and coordinates several agents to finish it. IBM describes a conductor model that supervises simpler agents. Sources: Google Cloud: What is agentic AI?, IBM: What is agentic AI?, Workday: AI agents vs agentic AI, ISACA: AI agents and agentic AI, arXiv: AI Agents vs. Agentic AI (Sapkota, Roumeliotis, Karkee).

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"AI agent vs agentic AI: the difference in plain words, with examples","dek":"An AI agent does one task on its own. Agentic AI plans a goal and coordinates agents to reach it. Here is how to tell them apart and which one you need.","summary":"An AI agent is software that performs a specific task on its own, while agentic AI is a system that sets a goal, plans the steps and coordinates several agents with little supervision. Google Cloud, IBM and ISACA draw the line in similar places, and ISACA advises using the simplest option that works.","seo_title":"AI agent vs agentic AI: the difference in plain words","seo_description":"AI agent vs agentic AI explained: the 4 real differences, where experts disagree, when to pick each one, and 3 prompts to sort your own work into agent tasks.","answer_summary":"An AI agent performs one specific task on its own. Agentic AI is a larger system that sets a goal, plans the steps and coordinates one or more agents to reach it with limited human supervision.","tags":["AI agents","Agentic AI","Google Cloud","IBM","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"AI agent vs agentic AI sounds like a word game, but the two terms describe different things. An AI agent is a piece of software built to do a specific task on its own. Agentic AI is the bigger system: it sets a goal, plans the steps, and coordinates one or more agents to get there with little human help. That is how Google Cloud and IBM both describe it on their own explainer pages.","sources":[{"name":"Google Cloud: What is agentic AI?","url":"https://cloud.google.com/discover/what-is-agentic-ai"},{"name":"IBM: What is agentic AI?","url":"https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/agentic-ai"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google Cloud puts it in one line: an AI agent might focus on a specific task, while agentic AI employs multiple agents to handle complex workflows. Google's comparison is a toolbox. The agents are the individual tools, and agentic AI is the coordinated use of those tools to finish a job.","sources":[{"name":"Google Cloud: What is agentic AI?","url":"https://cloud.google.com/discover/what-is-agentic-ai"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"AI agent vs agentic AI: the short definitions","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"AI agent: Google Cloud calls agents autonomous entities designed to perform specific tasks. Workday, the HR and finance software company, describes them as task oriented systems that carry out predefined actions within a workflow, such as answering an HR question or checking finance data. They act when given an instruction and do not plan ahead on their own.","sources":[{"name":"Google Cloud: What is agentic AI?","url":"https://cloud.google.com/discover/what-is-agentic-ai"},{"name":"Workday: AI agents vs agentic AI","url":"https://www.workday.com/en-gb/perspectives/ai/understanding-the-difference-between-ai-agents-and-agentic-ai.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Agentic AI: IBM defines it as an AI system that can accomplish a specific goal with limited supervision, and says it is made of AI agents. Google Cloud describes it as focused on autonomous decision making and action: it can set goals, plan and carry out tasks with minimal human intervention, using a large language model as the brain and acting through tools.","sources":[{"name":"Google Cloud: What is agentic AI?","url":"https://cloud.google.com/discover/what-is-agentic-ai"},{"name":"IBM: What is agentic AI?","url":"https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/agentic-ai"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Workday's shorthand is the easiest to remember: agentic AI is the thinker, AI agents are the doers. A 2025 research paper by Ranjan Sapkota, Konstantinos Roumeliotis and Manoj Karkee draws the line in a similar place. It treats AI agents as single, task specific systems and agentic AI as several specialized agents that coordinate, with shared memory and task breakdown.","sources":[{"name":"Workday: AI agents vs agentic AI","url":"https://www.workday.com/en-gb/perspectives/ai/understanding-the-difference-between-ai-agents-and-agentic-ai.html"},{"name":"arXiv: AI Agents vs. Agentic AI (Sapkota, Roumeliotis, Karkee)","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2505.10468v4"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The 4 differences that actually matter","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Scope: one task or one goal","text":"An agent does one job well: sort the support ticket, pull the invoice, draft the reply. An agentic system starts from a goal, such as resolving a customer complaint end to end, and decides which tasks it needs. Google Cloud's list of uses for agentic AI includes customer service, supply chains and software development.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Planning: follow steps or make them","text":"Workday says plainly that agents do not plan ahead and do not choose between alternatives. Agentic AI breaks a goal into steps and picks the order. IBM describes this as a goal setting stage that uses planning methods before the system acts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Coordination: alone or as a team","text":"IBM describes multiagent systems where each agent handles one subtask and their work is coordinated through orchestration. One design it describes uses a conductor model, powered by an LLM, that supervises simpler agents. A single agent has no one to coordinate with.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Learning: same every time or improving","text":"IBM lists learning and adaptation as a step in how agentic systems work, using feedback from earlier results. Google Cloud calls the same stage reflection. ISACA lists memory and knowledge management among the parts an agentic system needs.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where the experts disagree","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Not everyone uses the words the same way, and you will see it in product pages. ISACA, the IT governance association, points out that being an agent does not automatically mean being autonomous. A basic customer service chatbot is technically an agent but has no real agency. In ISACA's framing, agentic AI is defined by agency, the ability to act on its own, rather than by the number of agents.","sources":[{"name":"ISACA: AI agents and agentic AI","url":"https://isaca.org/resources/news-and-trends/isaca-now-blog/2025/ai-agents-and-agentic-ai-understanding-the-difference-that-matters-for-your-organization"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"So when a company says its product is agentic, ask what it actually decides on its own. If it only runs a fixed script after you press a button, it is an agent, or simply automation, whatever the marketing says.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Which one you need for your work","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"ISACA's advice is practical: use the simplest solution that works, and it says that might mean not building agentic systems at all. Simpler agents are more cost effective. IBM adds the risks that come with more autonomy: a system rewarded for a score can exploit loopholes to hit it in ways nobody intended, and when many agents work together one failure can cascade through the rest.","sources":[{"name":"ISACA: AI agents and agentic AI","url":"https://isaca.org/resources/news-and-trends/isaca-now-blog/2025/ai-agents-and-agentic-ai-understanding-the-difference-that-matters-for-your-organization"},{"name":"IBM: What is agentic AI?","url":"https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/agentic-ai"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"Pick an agent when","text":"The task is the same every time, the steps are known, and a mistake is easy to spot. Examples: tagging emails, filling a form from a document, answering a set list of HR questions.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"Pick an agentic system when","text":"The goal is clear but the path is not, the job crosses several apps, and the work is worth the extra checking. Examples: researching a topic across many sources, handling a support case from start to refund, or a coding task that needs planning, editing and testing.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Keep a human in the loop either way. Google Cloud's own page recommends human oversight for agentic AI, and ISACA notes that autonomy reduces the need for supervision but does not remove it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"3 prompts to sort your own work","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Split a job into agent tasks","text":"Here is a task I do every week: [describe the task in 3 to 5 sentences]. Break it into the smallest separate steps. For each step, tell me: is the input always the same format, does it need a judgment call, and what would go wrong if an AI got it wrong. Then group the steps into ones a simple AI agent could do and ones that need a person or a planning system.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Test an agentic claim","text":"A vendor says this product is agentic: [paste the product description]. Based only on this text, list what the product decides on its own, what it does only when a person tells it to, and what tools or apps it can act in. Say which parts are unclear and give me 5 questions to ask the vendor.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Plan the checks","text":"I want an AI system to handle this goal with little supervision: [describe the goal]. List the points where it should stop and ask me before acting, the actions it should never take on its own, and how I would notice if it took a shortcut to look successful.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The useful takeaway is simple. AI agent describes a worker with one job. Agentic AI describes a system that plans and runs a whole job, often with several of those workers. Both terms are stretched in marketing, so judge a product by what it decides on its own, not by the label.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How the Mercor AI interview works, and how to prepare
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The Practice Interview is free, can be repeated and is never shown to companies. The real one takes about 20 minutes. Use Chrome on a computer. A working mic is required, plus full screen sharing when asked. Face in frame and good light make a clear recording. Long silences make the AI jump in. If it cuts you off, say you were not finished. Using an AI to write your answers is banned. Sources: Mercor docs: AI Interview, Mercor docs: Apply for a Job, Mercor docs: How Mercor Uses AI and Data, Mercor blog: Engineering Monty.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to pass the Mercor AI interview: setup, rules, retakes and what happens to your data","dek":"Mercor screens every candidate with an AI interviewer called Monty. Here is how it works, what to set up first, what is banned, and how the three retakes work.","summary":"Mercor's AI interviewer asks role specific questions built from your resume and the job description, and most interviews take about 20 minutes. It is the only screening method, you get up to three retakes, and only your latest attempt is evaluated.","seo_title":"How to pass the Mercor AI interview: setup, rules and retakes","seo_description":"How the Mercor AI interview works: the free practice run, the setup checks, what AI help is banned, how the three retakes work and what Mercor keeps.","answer_summary":"The Mercor AI interview is a roughly 20 minute conversation with an AI interviewer that asks questions based on your resume and the role. Take the free practice interview, use Chrome on a computer with a working mic and camera, answer clearly, and save your three retakes for technical problems.","tags":["Mercor","AI interview","AI jobs","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to pass the Mercor AI interview starts with knowing what it is. Mercor is a hiring platform that matches experts with paid projects, and its help center says every candidate is screened by an AI interviewer that asks questions about the role, makes a transcript and scores your answers for that listing. Most interviews take about 20 minutes, and you only need to finish each one once.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"There is no human alternative. Mercor's docs say the AI interview is the only screening method, and it cannot be done by chat, phone call or any other format. Mercor's engineering blog names the interviewer Monty and says it runs around 10,000 conversations a day, about fifteen minutes each on average, across hundreds of job categories.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"},{"name":"Mercor docs: Apply for a Job","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/how-to/apply"},{"name":"Mercor blog: Engineering Monty","url":"https://www.mercor.com/blog/monty-engineering-deep-dive/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the Mercor AI interview asks you","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Mercor, the interviewer builds its questions from your resume and the job description, then transcribes and evaluates what you say. Some interviews are technical, others test language or reasoning. The blog post adds that the most common one, a general Domain Expert interview, makes up more than 70% of sessions, and that coding problems are generated from your profile.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"},{"name":"Mercor docs: How Mercor Uses AI and Data","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/policies/data-ai-usage"},{"name":"Mercor blog: Engineering Monty","url":"https://www.mercor.com/blog/monty-engineering-deep-dive/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"If you pass an interview, the result carries over. Mercor calls this assessment reuse: a passed assessment does not need to be taken again for comparable roles, and a finished interview is kept when another application asks for the same one.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"},{"name":"Mercor docs: Apply for a Job","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/how-to/apply"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Before you start: setup that actually matters","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Do the free practice interview","text":"Mercor offers a Practice Interview that is not tied to any application, does not affect your chances and can be repeated as often as you like. Practice interviews are not shared with companies, so use one to get used to the format.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Use Chrome on a computer","text":"Mercor recommends the latest Google Chrome. Edge and Safari are supported, Firefox is not. Some interviews need a computer; on a phone you will see a message saying the interview needs one, with a button to copy the link and open it on a laptop.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Pass the setup checks","text":"In the waiting room, the Setup checks tab tests your devices. Working mic is required, and so is screen sharing when the interview asks for it (share your entire screen, not one tab). Face in frame, good lighting, a working camera and a steady camera are not required, but Mercor says you need them for a clear recording. If Start interview stays gray, one required check has failed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Pick a quiet room","text":"Mercor suggests a quiet space, a stable connection, headphones and an external mic. Keep your whole face visible. Interviews are in English unless the listing says otherwise. Pen and paper help, plus a calculator for number heavy roles.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"During the interview","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Speak clearly and keep answers tight. Mercor warns that long silences can make the AI jump in. If it interrupts you while you are thinking, the docs say you can simply tell it you were not finished.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Captions are on by default and can be turned off. Some interviews include a whiteboard that saves on its own. If something breaks, use the Help button inside the interview. If the bot stops answering, Mercor's checklist is to wait 30 to 60 seconds, refresh and rejoin, clear Chrome's cached files and cookies, and turn off VPNs, ad blockers and privacy extensions.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On AI help, the rules are strict. Mercor's LLM usage policy, as summarized in its interview FAQ, allows grammar and wording checks but bans using large language models to write your answers, rate model responses, write explanations or review code. The docs also ask candidates not to share specific questions or screenshots of the interview.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Retakes: you get three","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"You can retake an interview up to three times across all applications that use it. Open the Assessments tab, click Retake assessment on the interview card, pick a reason (the options include Technical issue, Interrupted and Improve performance) and click Retake interview. Only your most recent attempt is evaluated, and retaking resets your application progress.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"},{"name":"Mercor docs: Apply for a Job","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/how-to/apply"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Save retakes for real problems. Mercor's own waiting room note says hiring managers can see how many times you retook an interview. An attempt that ends far too early is marked Interview too short and does not count, but retaking it still uses one of your three.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"After you submit","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Your application shows Ready to submit or Submitted for each step. Mercor gives no timeline for results; you are told when the application moves to the next stage, and you can keep applying elsewhere. Mercor says it cannot give specific feedback on rejections because of volume, and a submitted application cannot be edited or withdrawn.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"},{"name":"Mercor docs: Apply for a Job","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/how-to/apply"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On data, Mercor keeps the video, audio and transcript of official interviews to judge your candidacy and recommend you to employers, and says it does not sell interview data. Its FAQ says interview data will not be used to train AI models; its data policy says the data does train Mercor's internal recommendation models but never third party language models. You cannot download your recording or transcript. You can delete your account and its data in Account Settings, unless you have an active contract, a payout in progress or an open offer.","sources":[{"name":"Mercor docs: AI Interview","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/support/ai-interview"},{"name":"Mercor docs: How Mercor Uses AI and Data","url":"https://talent.docs.mercor.com/policies/data-ai-usage"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The honest read: there is no trick to beat the Mercor AI interview. The interviewer works from your resume, so the best preparation is a clean, text based PDF resume that states your real experience, one practice run, and a setup that passes every check. Mercor's own resume rules ask for a PDF under 2 MB, one or two pages, with no images or tables.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: NotebookLM vs Gemini: which one to use for your files
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Gemini Notebook answers only from the files you upload, with citations. Use it when a made up fact would hurt you. The Gemini app opens the same notebooks but may also use web search and other tools. Use it for anything your files do not cover. Sources: Gemini Notebook Help: Notebooks in Gemini Apps, Gemini Apps Help: notebooks in Gemini Apps, Gemini Notebook Help: Learn about Gemini Notebook, Gemini Notebook Help: usage limits, Gemini Notebook Help: Create a notebook, Gemini Notebook Help: Audio Overview, Gemini Notebook Help: Flashcards or Quizzes, Chalkbox.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"NotebookLM vs Gemini: which one to use for your files, and when to use both","dek":"NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook, and its notebooks also open in the Gemini app. One answers only from your sources, the other can add the web.","summary":"Gemini Notebook, the new name for NotebookLM, answers only from the sources in a notebook and holds the Studio tools such as Audio Overviews and flashcards. The Gemini app opens the same notebooks but may also use web search and other tools.","seo_title":"NotebookLM vs Gemini: which one to use, and when to use both","seo_description":"NotebookLM vs Gemini explained: what Gemini Notebook does that the Gemini app cannot, how shared notebooks sync, the steps for each, and the usage limits.","answer_summary":"Use Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM) when answers must come only from your files and you want Audio Overviews, flashcards or quizzes. Use the Gemini app when you want your notebook plus web search.","tags":["Gemini Notebook","NotebookLM","Gemini","Google","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"NotebookLM vs Gemini comes down to one choice: answers only from your own files, or answers that may also use the web. Google's help pages now call NotebookLM Gemini Notebook, an AI research assistant that answers from the sources you upload, with in-line citations. The Gemini app is the general assistant, and since this year it can open the same notebooks.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/17003757?hl=en"},{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Learn about Gemini Notebook","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16164461"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short version: use Gemini Notebook when the answer must stay inside your documents and you want study tools like Audio Overviews, flashcards and quizzes. Use the Gemini app when you want to mix your notebook with web search and Gemini's other tools. The notebooks themselves are shared between the two apps, so you do not have to pick only one.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/17003757?hl=en"},{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16972047"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"NotebookLM vs Gemini: the one difference that matters","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google's own help page states it plainly. In Gemini Notebook, answers are grounded only in your notebook sources. In the Gemini app, answers are grounded in your notebook sources but may also include web search and other tools. Gemini Notebook is designed to answer from the information in what you uploaded, and every answer carries citations you can click back to the source.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/17003757?hl=en"},{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Learn about Gemini Notebook","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16164461"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Chalkbox, a study site that tested both, sums it up the same way: the notebook answers only from your sources, the app answers from everything. It also adds a fair warning: grounding cuts down on made up facts, but the model can still misread a document. Check the citation before you quote anything.","sources":[{"name":"Chalkbox","url":"https://www.chalkbox.org/guides/notebooklm-vs-gemini/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"That makes the choice easy in practice. Writing about assigned readings, a contract, or meeting notes where a made up fact would hurt you: Gemini Notebook. Explaining a concept your files do not cover, or checking something against the current web: the Gemini app.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How notebooks work across both apps","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Notebooks you create in Gemini Notebook now show up automatically in the Gemini app's navigation, and you can view, edit and chat with them from either side. Renaming a notebook, adding sources, or changing its custom instructions syncs between the two apps. If a change does not show up, Google suggests refreshing. Both apps share one set of custom instructions per notebook.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/17003757?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"There are a few catches. Shared notebooks made in Gemini Notebook, even ones you own, do not appear in the Gemini app. A notebook that contains Gemini chats is private and cannot be shared. Play Books ebooks can only be added as sources in Gemini Notebook. In the European Economic Area you have to connect Gemini Notebook to Gemini by hand; in most other regions it connects automatically.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/17003757?hl=en"},{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16972047"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What only Gemini Notebook can do","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Studio panel is the big reason to open Gemini Notebook itself. Google lists Notes, Audio Overviews, Video Overviews, Mind Maps, Reports (FAQ, study guide or briefing document, with Export to Docs), Data Tables (Export to Sheets), Flashcards, Quizzes, Slide Decks and Infographics. The Gemini app cannot generate these Studio items: Google says they are only available in Gemini Notebook.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/17003757?hl=en"},{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Create a notebook","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16206563"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Audio Overviews turn your sources into a discussion between AI hosts. You can pick Deep Dive (the default), The Brief (one speaker, under two minutes), The Critique or The Debate, choose the length, and add a prompt about what to focus on. In English you can also use Interactive mode and join the conversation to ask questions. It works in more than 80 languages.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Audio Overview","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16212820"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Flashcards and Quizzes turn your sources into study aids. You can set the difficulty to easy, medium or hard, choose fewer, standard or more cards, and add a prompt. Flashcards have Got it! and Missed it! buttons, so you can review only the cards you missed, and you can download the deck as a CSV file.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Flashcards or Quizzes","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16958963"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the Gemini app adds","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In the Gemini app, a notebook chat can use web searches and any Gemini tool, and Gemini remembers the context of your sources and instructions. You can ask Gemini in plain words to create, edit or delete notebooks, add or remove sources, or list your notebooks. Sources can be files from your device (PDFs, documents, spreadsheets, images, audio and text files), Google Drive files, websites and copied text. Google says you can add up to 600 sources, depending on your Google AI plan.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16972047"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Gemini app also has study notebooks on the web at gemini.google.com, with diagnostic quizzes, personalized lessons and progress tracking. They need Gemini Apps Activity (History) turned on and are not yet in the mobile app.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: notebooks in Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16972047"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to start a notebook in each app","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Gemini Notebook: create the notebook","text":"Open Gemini Notebook and select Create new notebook. In the pop up, select Upload a source. You can add PDFs, websites, YouTube videos, audio files, Google Docs or Google Slides. Add more later with the + Add button.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Gemini Notebook: open Studio","text":"Once your sources are in, use the Chat panel for questions and the Studio panel on the side for Audio Overviews, Mind Maps, Reports, Flashcards or Quizzes. A few starter items are made automatically when you first add sources, and Google says those do not count toward your limits.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Gemini app: make a notebook","text":"On gemini.google.com or in the Gemini mobile app, tap Menu at the top left, then New notebook under Notebooks. Give it a name, type a prompt and tap Add sources.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Gemini app: talk to an existing notebook","text":"Type @Gemini Notebook in a prompt to connect the app the first time, then ask about any notebook by name. To file a normal Gemini chat into a notebook, open More, then Add to notebook. This needs Keep Activity turned on.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Check a claim against your files only (Gemini Notebook)","text":"Using only my sources, list every place that mentions [topic]. For each one, quote the key sentence and say which source it is from. If my sources do not cover it, say so instead of guessing.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Mix your notes with the web (Gemini app)","text":"Read my notebook [notebook name]. item.title: Nvidia just stopped shipping AI servers to four Asian countries
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Dell and Supermicro told customers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia that Nvidia will not authorize their orders, the FT reports. Nvidia declined to comment. New US rules give regional cloud providers 90 days to get export licenses and prove no restricted users. The target: Chinese developers renting Nvidia compute nearby. Sources: The National, Lowyat.NET.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"Nvidia halts AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries, report says","dek":"Dell and Supermicro told customers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia that Nvidia will not authorize their orders as new US cloud rules take effect.","summary":"Nvidia told its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers with its AI chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported on November 26, 2026. The move follows new US rules that give regional cloud providers 90 days to obtain export licenses.","seo_title":"Nvidia halts AI server shipments to Southeast Asia, FT says","seo_description":"Nvidia paused AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after new US rules gave cloud providers 90 days to get export licenses.","answer_summary":"Nvidia asked server makers such as Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping its AI servers to four Southeast Asian countries while it works out how to comply with new US export rules aimed at Chinese access to rented computing power.","tags":["Nvidia","Export controls","Data centers","Southeast Asia","Jensen Huang"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Nvidia has told the companies that build its servers to stop shipping systems with its AI chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported on November 26, 2026, citing three people familiar with the matter. The report was carried by The National and the Malaysian tech site Lowyat.NET.","sources":[{"name":"The National","url":"https://www.thenationalnews.com/future/technology/2026/11/26/nvidia-halts-chip-shipments-to-south-east-asia-amid-us-crackdown/"},{"name":"Lowyat.NET","url":"https://www.lowyat.net/2026/410482/nvidia-halts-ai-server-malaysia/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to the report, server makers including Dell and Supermicro have informed customers in the four countries that Nvidia will not authorize their pending orders to be shipped. It is not clear whether the pause is temporary or how long it could last. The sources said Nvidia and its manufacturing partners are trying to work out how to comply with the latest United States export rules.","sources":[{"name":"The National","url":"https://www.thenationalnews.com/future/technology/2026/11/26/nvidia-halts-chip-shipments-to-south-east-asia-amid-us-crackdown/"},{"name":"Lowyat.NET","url":"https://www.lowyat.net/2026/410482/nvidia-halts-ai-server-malaysia/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Nvidia declined to comment on the suspension, Lowyat.NET reported, and Dell and Supermicro did not respond to the Financial Times.","sources":[{"name":"Lowyat.NET","url":"https://www.lowyat.net/2026/410482/nvidia-halts-ai-server-malaysia/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Why the four countries matter","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia have become popular destinations for Chinese AI developers looking for Nvidia's most advanced processors, which Washington bars from direct export to China, both outlets said. One common route has been to rent computing power from cloud providers outside mainland China, which buy servers built around Nvidia chips and lease out the capacity.","sources":[{"name":"The National","url":"https://www.thenationalnews.com/future/technology/2026/11/26/nvidia-halts-chip-shipments-to-south-east-asia-amid-us-crackdown/"},{"name":"Lowyat.NET","url":"https://www.lowyat.net/2026/410482/nvidia-halts-ai-server-malaysia/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The shipment halt follows new rules introduced by the US Commerce Department the previous week to close that route. A cloud provider executive in the region told the Financial Times that companies do not know how to apply for the license before the deadline and that the new rule came without guidance on how to carry it out.","sources":[{"name":"The National","url":"https://www.thenationalnews.com/future/technology/2026/11/26/nvidia-halts-chip-shipments-to-south-east-asia-amid-us-crackdown/"},{"name":"Lowyat.NET","url":"https://www.lowyat.net/2026/410482/nvidia-halts-ai-server-malaysia/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What is at stake for Nvidia","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Southeast Asia's growing data center industry has become an important source of revenue for Nvidia. Company accounts cited by the Financial Times show Nvidia booked $104 billion in revenue through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, up 72 percent from a year earlier, according to The National. Nvidia also records some revenue from Taiwan and China through that unit, so the figure is not all regional sales.","sources":[{"name":"The National","url":"https://www.thenationalnews.com/future/technology/2026/11/26/nvidia-halts-chip-shipments-to-south-east-asia-amid-us-crackdown/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has argued in the past that allowing the company to sell chips in China would keep the country dependent on American technology, The National noted.","sources":[{"name":"The National","url":"https://www.thenationalnews.com/future/technology/2026/11/26/nvidia-halts-chip-shipments-to-south-east-asia-amid-us-crackdown/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The halt shows how far the latest controls reach beyond China itself. By targeting rented computing power, Washington has made ordinary server orders in neighboring countries a compliance risk, and Nvidia appears to be pausing first and sorting out the paperwork later. For data center builders in the region, a 90 day licensing clock with no clear process means projects can stall even when the end customer has nothing to do with China.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"Watch whether the Commerce Department publishes guidance on the new cloud licenses before the 90 day window closes, and whether Nvidia resumes shipments to customers who can show they qualify.","sources":[]}]}

On the free plan you get a JPEG at the original size; PNG, WEBP and larger sizes need a paid plan.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to get readable text in Ideogram images","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The docs give one main rule: put any text you want in the image in quotation marks, near the start of the prompt, spelled and capitalized exactly as you want it. English gives the most reliable results, especially with text. Ideogram does not treat weights or flags such as --ar as commands, so set the aspect ratio and quality in the panel instead.","sources":[{"name":"Ideogram docs: Prompting basics","url":"https://docs.ideogram.ai/prompting/prompting"},{"name":"Ideogram docs: Create images","url":"https://docs.ideogram.ai/create/create"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A poster with a clear headline","text":"A poster that says \"[YOUR HEADLINE]\" in bold letters at the top, [SUBJECT] below it, [STYLE] style, plenty of empty space around the text","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A thumbnail with two lines of text","text":"A video thumbnail with the words \"[LINE ONE]\" in large white letters and \"[LINE TWO]\" in smaller yellow letters, [SUBJECT] on the right side, bright background","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Words in your prompt can show up in the picture even when you did not want them there. Keep descriptions plain and put only the text you want shown inside quotation marks.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The settings that matter","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Magic Prompt is a toggle that starts on. The docs say it rewrites your prompt for more variety and richness and can translate it into English; turn it off when you want the model to follow your exact words. It is hidden on the newest models when reference images are attached, and the Auto model has no Magic Prompt.","sources":[{"name":"Ideogram docs: Image settings","url":"https://docs.ideogram.ai/create/image-settings"},{"name":"MindStudio: What is Ideogram","url":"https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/ideogram"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Ideogram 4.6 is the newest model in the docs, which suggest starting there for new work. You can make Auto or 1 to 8 images per run, and more images cost more credits. Quality changes the price too: on Ideogram 4.5 an image costs 3, 6 or 10 credits at Low, Medium or High, so lower quality stretches the free allowance further.","sources":[{"name":"Ideogram docs: Image settings","url":"https://docs.ideogram.ai/create/image-settings"},{"name":"Ideogram docs: Plans and credits","url":"https://docs.ideogram.ai/plans-and-billing/available-plans"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to fix a wrong word in Studio","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Studio, found under More in the sidebar, replaces the old Canvas and Magic Fill tools and saves your work automatically. The FAQ's fix for bad text is to regenerate with the exact words in quotes first. If only one word is wrong, edit it in Studio with AI edit, or use Layerize text to turn the text into layers you can retype. Select area, Extend, Remix and Upscale inside Studio need a paid plan.","sources":[{"name":"Ideogram docs: FAQ","url":"https://docs.ideogram.ai/help/frequently-asked-questions"},{"name":"Ideogram docs: Studio","url":"https://docs.ideogram.ai/edit/studio"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Ideogram costs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The free plan gives 30 credits a week, reset every Saturday at 00:00 UTC, plus 100 image descriptions a week and 10 edited images in total. Free images are public. Plus costs $20 a month, or $15 a month billed yearly, with 2,400 credits a month and private generation. Pro costs $60 a month with 7,500 credits, and Team costs $30 per user a month with at least 2 users. One credit equals one US cent of list price, and failed or blocked generations are not charged.","sources":[{"name":"Ideogram docs: Plans and credits","url":"https://docs.ideogram.ai/plans-and-billing/available-plans"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"The FAQ says there are no refunds and asks you to cancel at least 5 days before your renewal date. Set a reminder if you try a paid month.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Ideogram is worth a try when the words in a picture matter as much as the picture: a flyer, a sign, a cover, a thumbnail. The free plan is small, a handful of images a week at medium quality, and everything you make on it is public, so it is a test drive rather than a workhorse. If you need private images or regular output, Plus is the realistic starting point.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Gumloop to build an AI agent
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Click New agent, describe the job or pick a template, then add connectors like Gmail or Slack. Choose the model and click Save. Open the Triggers tab: an app event, a webhook, a schedule or a one-time run. Then the agent works without you starting it. Every task shows what it cost. One credit is half a cent. Start on Balanced or Auto and save the smartest model for hard jobs. Sources: Gumloop docs: Agents, Gumloop docs: Agent triggers, Gumloop docs: Credits, Gumloop pricing, Gumloop docs: AI models, DataCamp: Gumloop tutorial.

Create a new agent","text":"Select Agents in the navigation rail, then New agent in the Agents panel or Create Agent on the Agents page. If Gumloop asks where to create it, pick Personal or one of your teams.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Describe the job","text":"The guided setup asks what the agent should take care of. Describe the goal in plain words, pick a template, or select Start from scratch.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Add connectors","text":"In the Agent tab, open Connectors and click + Add. Pick only the apps this agent needs. The docs name Gmail, Salesforce, Slack and Notion among more than 300 connectors.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Pick the model","text":"Choose the model from the dropdown at the top of the Agent tab. Auto is a router that picks a model for each message, and there are Balanced and Smartest presets.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Run a first task","text":"Send a message in the chat to start a task and watch what the agent does. When it gets something wrong, correct it in the chat.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Make the fix stick","text":"Ask the agent to update your instructions, or to turn this into a skill. The docs are clear that feedback in one chat does not change future tasks on its own.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Save","text":"Click Save, or press Ctrl or Cmd + S, to keep configuration changes. The arrow next to Save undoes unsaved changes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Run it automatically with a trigger","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Triggers live in the Triggers tab of the agent's right panel. The docs list five kinds: App Trigger (an event in a connected app), Webhook, Scheduled Trigger, One-Time Trigger and Create With AI. A scheduled trigger can run as often as every minute, and polling app triggers check for new events about every 60 seconds.","sources":[{"name":"Gumloop docs: Agents","url":"https://docs.gumloop.com/core-concepts/agents"},{"name":"Gumloop docs: Agent triggers","url":"https://docs.gumloop.com/core-concepts/agent_triggers"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"8. Add a trigger","text":"Open the Triggers tab, choose a trigger type, give it a name and a prompt, and click Create trigger. If the agent already has triggers, select Add trigger first.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Write the trigger prompt as if the agent has never seen you before. The docs use a vague prompt like do the usual thing as an example of what not to write.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Webhook triggers accept up to 100 requests per minute, and anyone with the webhook URL can run the agent, so treat that URL like a password.","sources":[{"name":"Gumloop docs: Agent triggers","url":"https://docs.gumloop.com/core-concepts/agent_triggers"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Gumloop costs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The pricing page lists one self-serve plan, Pro, at $37 a month with 20,000 credits, unlimited agents, seats and teams, and a 14-day free trial; Enterprise is custom. The credits docs say the trial needs a card, is one time per customer and turns into paid Pro unless you cancel. Credits do not roll over, except on Enterprise.","sources":[{"name":"Gumloop pricing","url":"https://www.gumloop.com/pricing"},{"name":"Gumloop docs: Credits","url":"https://docs.gumloop.com/core-concepts/credits"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"One credit costs $0.005, so $1 buys 200 credits. A task pays for the model (the model cost divided by $0.005), 1 credit per successful connector call, and 5 credits per minute of compute, plus an 8 percent orchestration fee on top. Failed tool calls are not charged. If you run out, you can turn on overage billing at the same $0.005 per credit.","sources":[{"name":"Gumloop docs: Credits","url":"https://docs.gumloop.com/core-concepts/credits"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Bring your own API key (BYOK) needs Pro or higher. Eligible model calls then cost 0 model credits, and the orchestration fee rises to 16 percent.","sources":[{"name":"Gumloop docs: Credits","url":"https://docs.gumloop.com/core-concepts/credits"},{"name":"Gumloop docs: AI models","url":"https://docs.gumloop.com/core-concepts/ai_models"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to spend fewer credits","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Start on Balanced or Auto, and switch to Smartest only for the hard jobs. The credits docs give the same advice.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Start a new chat for a new topic. Long chats grow the context the model re-reads, and that is where credits go.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Set usage notifications early. By default Gumloop warns you at 75 and 90 percent of your credits.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Gumloop is a good fit if you want an agent that reacts to email, Slack or app events without writing code. It is a weaker fit if you need a free plan or a fixed monthly bill: the current pricing has no free tier, credits expire each month, and cost depends on model, chat length and tools. Build one agent with one trigger during the trial and check its credit use per task before you commit.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Lindy AI to build an assistant
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Open Routines, click New and type what you want, like a weekday summary of unread email. Lindy fills in the name, the trigger and the schedule. The Discover tab has ready routines: Morning briefing, Weekly wrap, Calendar audit and more. Each card says if it is ready or needs setup. Every seat shares one pool of credits. Admins can set a credit limit per person in Settings, Members. Sources: Lindy docs: Quickstart, Lindy docs: Pricing, Lindy docs: Usage, Lindy docs: Skills, Lindy docs: Routines, Lindy docs: Memory, Lindy docs: Integrations, Dupple: Lindy AI pricing.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Lindy AI: set up your assistant, routines and skills","dek":"Lindy works from Slack, email, calendar and text. Here is how to set it up, build your first routine, teach it a skill and keep credits under control.","summary":"Lindy is an AI assistant that completes work across connected tools, reached through Slack, email, iMessage or text. It is priced per user with a shared credit pool, starts with a free 7-day credit trial, and runs automations called routines.","seo_title":"How to use Lindy AI: setup, routines, skills and credits","seo_description":"How to use Lindy AI step by step: add it to Slack, connect email and calendar, build your first routine, teach it a skill and cut credit use. Plans explained.","answer_summary":"Add Lindy to Slack or sign up, connect your Google or Microsoft account and your phone, then open Routines, click New and describe the task in plain English. Lindy sets the trigger and schedule for you.","tags":["Lindy","AI assistant","Automation","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"If you want to know how to use Lindy AI, here is the short version: get Lindy into Slack or sign up on its own, connect your email, calendar and phone, then build routines that run on a schedule or when something happens. Lindy's docs describe it as an AI employee that completes work across your connected tools, working as a personal assistant for one person and as a shared teammate for a team.","sources":[{"name":"Lindy docs: Quickstart","url":"https://www.lindy.ai/docs/start-here/quickstart"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"You talk to it through Slack DMs, email, iMessage or text, and you can @mention it in shared Slack channels. The docs list Gmail, Slack, Notion, HubSpot, Google Drive and GitHub among more than 3,000 integrations, plus any MCP server. Microsoft Teams support is listed as coming soon.","sources":[{"name":"Lindy docs: Quickstart","url":"https://www.lindy.ai/docs/start-here/quickstart"},{"name":"Lindy docs: Integrations","url":"https://www.lindy.ai/docs/integrations/overview"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to set up Lindy AI","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Add Lindy to Slack","text":"For a team, an admin installs Lindy from Slack's Add to Slack screen. The first time a teammate DMs or @mentions Lindy, it replies with a Connect Slack to Lindy button. One tap and a confirm links that person. The quickstart says the whole setup takes about two minutes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Connect email and calendar","text":"Connect a Google or Microsoft account. This is what lets Lindy read your inbox, prep and take notes for meetings, and schedule for you.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Add your phone","text":"Add a phone number or connect Apple Messages, then verify it with a code. After that you can text Lindy like a person.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Connect your other tools","text":"Search for a tool on the integrations page and connect it with OAuth or an API key. Every action for that tool turns on at once. You can add more than one account for the same tool, for example two Gmail inboxes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Test it with a simple ask","text":"The quickstart suggests starting with plain requests such as asking what is on your calendar today, or asking it to schedule 30 minutes with a colleague next week.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Build your first routine","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A routine is an automation attached to your Lindy. Each one has three parts: a trigger (when it runs), a prompt in plain English (what to do) and a destination (where the result goes). Triggers can be a schedule, daily, weekly or monthly, or an event such as an email arriving, a Slack message, a calendar event about to start or a meeting ending. A Smart Filter narrows event triggers in plain English.","sources":[{"name":"Lindy docs: Routines","url":"https://www.lindy.ai/docs/teammate/routines"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Open Routines and click New","text":"Open Routines from the left sidebar and click New. Type into the Describe your routine box, for example: every weekday at 9, summarize my unread email and Slack mentions. Lindy fills in the name, the trigger and the schedule. Use Advanced settings if you want to set them by hand.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Or start from a template","text":"The Discover tab has ready routines such as Morning briefing, End-of-day review, Weekly wrap, Promise tracker, Post-meeting follow-ups, Calendar audit and Channel digest. Each card shows Ready, Needs setup or Needs admin.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"8. Do a dry run first","text":"Before you let a routine loose, ask Lindy in chat for a dry run, for example: Dry-run my morning briefing. Nothing gets sent. New routines run daily at 9:00 AM until you change the schedule.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Personal routines deliver to your default channel, Lindy chat, text or a Slack DM. Workspace routines post to a Slack thread or a channel, and only admins can create them. Lindy also ships built-in routines you switch on per account, including daily briefs, email drafting, email labeling, urgent email alerts, follow-up bumps, meeting recording, meeting prep and meeting scheduling.","sources":[{"name":"Lindy docs: Routines","url":"https://www.lindy.ai/docs/teammate/routines"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Teach Lindy a skill","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A skill is a playbook you teach Lindy: named instructions for a procedure you repeat. You can describe the process in chat and Lindy saves it as a skill, create one on the Skills page, or record your screen with Watch and Learn. Lindy always sees skill names and descriptions and loads the full instructions only when a request calls for it.","sources":[{"name":"Lindy docs: Skills","url":"https://www.lindy.ai/docs/teammate/skills"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If Lindy ignores a skill, rewrite its description to be more specific. The docs say the description is what Lindy uses to pick the right skill.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lindy keeps its files in Memory, a page in the left sidebar where you can read and edit them. Files come in Personal, Team and System scopes, and every save is a new version, so you can check what Lindy has learned and fix it.","sources":[{"name":"Lindy docs: Memory","url":"https://www.lindy.ai/docs/teammate/memory"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Lindy AI costs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lindy charges per user, and everyone in a workspace shares one pool of credits. The docs list Plus, Pro and Max plans plus Enterprise, and say credits cost $0.01 each on base plans. You start with free credits and no credit card; they last 7 days and the free week is one time per person. Plan credits reset each billing cycle and do not roll over, while top-up credits carry over. Phone calls start at 25 credits per minute.","sources":[{"name":"Lindy docs: Pricing","url":"https://www.lindy.ai/docs/pricing"},{"name":"Lindy docs: Usage","url":"https://www.lindy.ai/docs/account-billing/usage"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The docs send you to Settings, Billing for current prices. Dupple, reading Lindy's pricing page in November 2026, reported a seat starting at $49.99 a month for 5,000 credits, with larger rungs of 15,000 credits for $99.99 and 35,000 for $199.99.","sources":[{"name":"Dupple: Lindy AI pricing","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/lindy-ai-pricing"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Watch the seat count. Per the docs, anyone who signs up, joins the workspace or @mentions Lindy in Slack takes a billed seat.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to spend fewer credits","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lindy's usage page gives its own advice. Start a new thread for a new topic, because each message re-reads everything above it. Be specific: five bullets on a company's funding history costs less than a vague research ask. Pick a cheaper model for summaries and drafts from the dropdown below the taskbar. Review team routines monthly, and turn off the ones nobody reads.","sources":[{"name":"Lindy docs: Usage","url":"https://www.lindy.ai/docs/account-billing/usage"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Set a cap per person in Settings, Members: click the menu on a row and choose Edit credit limit. When someone hits it, their credit-using actions pause.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Lindy is strongest as an inbox, calendar and meeting assistant for people who already live in Slack. It is weaker as a cheap solo tool: billing is per seat, credits vanish at the end of each cycle, and the docs do not publish prices outside the app. Run the free week on one routine you would really use every day before you pay.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Devin, the AI software engineer
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Switch to Ask, pick your repo and ask how the code works. Ask mode never changes code. Then click Construct a Devin Prompt and Send to Devin. In Agent mode, choose the repository and the agent: Lite for chores, Normal by default, Ultra for the hardest work. Devin opens the pull request and watches CI. Sources: Devin docs: Introducing Devin, Devin docs: Your First Session, Devin docs: Self-serve plans, Cognition blog: New self-serve plans for Devin.

Set up your repository first","text":"Before the first session, the docs tell you to add and index your repository and set up its environment. Start in Ask mode","text":"On the main page, switch the toggle to Ask and pick one or more repositories. Point Devin at the right context","text":"Type @ in the message box to mention repos, files, sessions, skills, secrets or Knowledge entries. item.title: Ex-OpenAI researcher's AI fund lost 65% in one quarter
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Situational Awareness, the hedge fund of former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, told investors it lost 65% after fees in the third quarter, the WSJ reported. item.title: How to use Jules, Google's coding agent
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Sign in at jules.google.com, connect GitHub, pick a repo and branch, then describe the task. Click Give me a plan. Jules works in its own cloud VM. item.title: Anthropic: 1 in 5 AI rollouts deliver nothing yet
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic's economists interviewed 66 people at 58 US companies about nearly 300 AI uses. 55% reported higher output or quality. 19% have brought no business value so far. The top obstacle, named 49 times, was more AI output than people could check. Employee resistance came next with 43 mentions, then required expert reviews with 42. Sources: The Decoder, AI Daily Post, Today for AI.

item.title: Google's AI agent wrote six math papers in one day, including a 34-year-old factoring problem
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On November 25, Google Research added six papers to its public GitHub, each written by its Cogentic agent on Gemini 4. Google's files say no human stepped in beyond the first prompt. The lead paper claims a fully proven L[1/3] speed for factoring any whole number. The best proven bound since 1992 was L[1/2]. Its constant is 105, far above today's best method, so RSA is not weaker. None of the six papers is peer reviewed. Lean 4 proofs that a computer can check are promised but not public. Sources: Snape Report, Apple Scoop, CellCog.

Snape Report likewise said the bound does not speed up attacks on RSA.","sources":[{"name":"Snape Report","url":"https://snapereport.com/s/google-cogentic-agent-posts-six-math-papers-led-by-claimed-fast-factoring-proof"},{"name":"Apple Scoop","url":"https://applescoop.org/story/did-ai-break-encryption-google-cogentic-factoring-openai-matrix-9-4"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A second factoring paper claims a deterministic method, one that uses no randomness, at a slower subexponential bound, and also covers the construction of quadratic nonresidues. A third paper claims a faster proven algorithm for discrete logarithms in finite fields of small characteristic, improving on quasi-polynomial results from 2022 and 2026. Apple Scoop said those small-characteristic fields are not the ones used by modern security systems.","sources":[{"name":"Apple Scoop","url":"https://applescoop.org/story/did-ai-break-encryption-google-cogentic-factoring-openai-matrix-9-4"},{"name":"CellCog","url":"https://cellcog.ai/blog/google-cogentic-math-papers/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The other three papers","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to CellCog's summary of the folder, the remaining papers move beyond number theory. One claims an exact polynomial-time algorithm for 1/5-approximate Nash equilibria in two-player games, improving on a 1/3 guarantee. Another claims to break the square-root barrier for the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity, by a margin of five millionths in the exponent. The last claims that every simple graph with at least 1,000 times as many edges as vertices can be reconstructed from its edge-deleted subgraphs, extending a 1977 result. The papers run from 36 to 59 pages each.","sources":[{"name":"CellCog","url":"https://cellcog.ai/blog/google-cogentic-math-papers/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What has not been checked","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"None of the six papers has been peer reviewed, and no outside mathematician has said on record that the proofs are correct, according to Apple Scoop and CellCog. The README files say complete Lean 4 formalizations, which a computer can check line by line, have been finished and will be released in a companion submission. Those files were not public on November 25, Snape Report said.","sources":[{"name":"Snape Report","url":"https://snapereport.com/s/google-cogentic-agent-posts-six-math-papers-led-by-claimed-fast-factoring-proof"},{"name":"Apple Scoop","url":"https://applescoop.org/story/did-ai-break-encryption-google-cogentic-factoring-openai-matrix-9-4"},{"name":"CellCog","url":"https://cellcog.ai/blog/google-cogentic-math-papers/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The volume is the striking part. Six long papers on open problems arriving on a single day from one prompt each is new for a research lab, but the value of each claim now depends on the formal proofs Google has promised. If the Lean files compile, the factoring paper would close a gap in the theory of algorithms that has been open for more than three decades, even though it changes nothing for practical cryptography.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The release of the Lean 4 formalizations, and the first reviews from number theorists and cryptographers, will show whether these six results hold up.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Epic CEO calls Claude garbage after it blocked his work
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney said on X on November 25 that Claude blocked set theory work he was doing and accused him of distillation. Distillation means using one AI's answers to train another model. He said the block came after 1 to 2 hours a day of prompting on a company account. "Anthropic can't keep sabotaging customers' work like this," he wrote. In a later reply he narrowed it: "The anti-distillation feature is garbage." He called Claude's top models "quite excellent overall." Anthropic had not responded publicly by that evening. Sources: TweakTown, WindowsForum, SSBCrack News.

item.title: An OpenAI model claims to end a math search that began in 1969: exactly 9/4
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In October, OpenAI showed matrices can be multiplied with an exponent of 9/4. The new preprint claims nothing can do better. That would rule out 2, the value many theorists expected. The preprint is not peer reviewed, and its Lean check covers only circuits that never divide. It is a result about circuit cost, so it will not make GPUs faster. Sources: alphaXiv: The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths, MadRobot, Let's Data Science.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"OpenAI preprint claims the matrix multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4","dek":"A new manuscript in OpenAI's math repository adds a matching lower bound to October's 9/4 upper bound, but it has not been peer reviewed and is only partly machine checked.","summary":"OpenAI has posted a preprint dated November 24, 2026 that claims the exponent of square matrix multiplication is exactly 9/4 over every field. What it says, what is checked and what is not yet.","answer_summary":"OpenAI claims that multiplying two n by n matrices needs on the order of n to the power 9/4 multiplications in the arithmetic circuit model, matching its October upper bound, but the proof is unreviewed and its Lean check covers only division free circuits.","tags":["OpenAI","Matrix multiplication","AI and mathematics","Lean","Research"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI has posted a preprint titled \"The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths\" to its public openai/math repository on GitHub, according to MadRobot and Let's Data Science. The manuscript is dated November 24, 2026, and its abstract page on alphaXiv, which lists OpenAI as the author, shows a submission date of November 25. The abstract states that the exponent of square matrix multiplication is 9/4 over every field.","sources":[{"name":"alphaXiv: The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths","url":"https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.matrix-multiplication-exponent-lower-bound"},{"name":"MadRobot","url":"https://madrobot.blog/2026/11/25/openai-matrix-multiplication-exponent-9-4-proof/"},{"name":"Let's Data Science","url":"https://letsdatascience.com/news/openai-preprint-claims-matrix-multiplication-exponent-is-exa-7997d3b1"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The matrix multiplication exponent, usually written as omega, describes how the cost of multiplying two n by n matrices grows as the matrices get larger. The schoolbook method takes on the order of n cubed steps, and no method can go below n squared, because the answer alone has that many entries. MadRobot notes that Volker Strassen's 1969 algorithm started the search for faster methods, that the best known exponent had reached about 2.371 by 2024, and that many theorists suspected the true value was 2.","sources":[{"name":"MadRobot","url":"https://madrobot.blog/2026/11/25/openai-matrix-multiplication-exponent-9-4-proof/"},{"name":"Let's Data Science","url":"https://letsdatascience.com/news/openai-preprint-claims-matrix-multiplication-exponent-is-exa-7997d3b1"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"From an upper bound to an exact answer","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The upper half of the claim is not new. According to Let's Data Science, an OpenAI preprint from October 2 showed that omega is at most 9/4 over the complex numbers. MadRobot reports that Rafael Pass later gave an independent constructive proof of that bound, and that Alimzhan Amanov, Maxim van den Berg and Jeroen Zuiddam extended it to every field. The alphaXiv abstract also credits the Amanov, van den Berg and Zuiddam paper for the upper bound over every field.","sources":[{"name":"alphaXiv: The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths","url":"https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.matrix-multiplication-exponent-lower-bound"},{"name":"MadRobot","url":"https://madrobot.blog/2026/11/25/openai-matrix-multiplication-exponent-9-4-proof/"},{"name":"Let's Data Science","url":"https://letsdatascience.com/news/openai-preprint-claims-matrix-multiplication-exponent-is-exa-7997d3b1"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The new contribution is the matching lower bound. The abstract says that for every n of at least 2, any formal arithmetic circuit that multiplies two n by n matrices needs at least n to the power 9/4, divided by two and rounded up, nonscalar multiplication or division gates, even if additions and other linear operations cost nothing. Put together with the upper bound, that would fix omega at exactly 2.25 and rule out the long held hope that it equals 2.","sources":[{"name":"alphaXiv: The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths","url":"https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.matrix-multiplication-exponent-lower-bound"},{"name":"MadRobot","url":"https://madrobot.blog/2026/11/25/openai-matrix-multiplication-exponent-9-4-proof/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"MadRobot describes the proof as an argument by contradiction: if omega were below 9/4, exact networks for a problem called list distinctness could be compressed far enough to break a known lower bound. The alphaXiv abstract describes the same approach and stresses that the result concerns circuit cost, not running time, hardware or any particular implementation.","sources":[{"name":"alphaXiv: The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths","url":"https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.matrix-multiplication-exponent-lower-bound"},{"name":"MadRobot","url":"https://madrobot.blog/2026/11/25/openai-matrix-multiplication-exponent-9-4-proof/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What has and has not been checked","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Both news reports say the work has not been peer reviewed, and MadRobot reports that no one outside OpenAI has checked the new proof and that no mathematician has commented on it publicly. The release includes a Lean formalization, but according to the alphaXiv abstract and MadRobot it covers only division free circuits, which is narrower than the model used in the manuscript, so the division case of the main theorem is not machine checked.","sources":[{"name":"alphaXiv: The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths","url":"https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.matrix-multiplication-exponent-lower-bound"},{"name":"MadRobot","url":"https://madrobot.blog/2026/11/25/openai-matrix-multiplication-exponent-9-4-proof/"},{"name":"Let's Data Science","url":"https://letsdatascience.com/news/openai-preprint-claims-matrix-multiplication-exponent-is-exa-7997d3b1"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"MadRobot quotes the repository as saying the manuscripts come from an unnamed internal OpenAI model, are best seen as raw research data rather than polished papers, and that some of the unformalized results could have issues. It also reports that OpenAI withdrew three papers from the same collection a day after posting them in October. All three sources note that the result is asymptotic and does not directly speed up GPU kernels or deep learning software.","sources":[{"name":"MadRobot","url":"https://madrobot.blog/2026/11/25/openai-matrix-multiplication-exponent-9-4-proof/"},{"name":"Let's Data Science","url":"https://letsdatascience.com/news/openai-preprint-claims-matrix-multiplication-exponent-is-exa-7997d3b1"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The claim lands one day after Anthropic posted a Claude written proof on the VP versus VNP question, which also came with partial machine checking and no human review. Both labs are now publishing results on classic open problems faster than mathematicians can read them, which shifts the bottleneck from finding proofs to verifying them. A lower bound that matches a known upper bound would be an unusually clean result for a question this old, and that is exactly why experts are likely to examine the parts that Lean does not cover.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next signal to watch is whether independent complexity theorists review the division case of the proof, or whether OpenAI extends the Lean formalization to cover it.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: OpenAI says GPT-6.2 designed proteins that really bound their targets in a lab
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: GPT-6.2 wrote code to shape small binding proteins for five targets. The lab partner Onava made and tested them. 35 bound, about 10.9 percent, with at least one hit on every target. When GPT-6.2 redesigned the binding loops of known antibodies, 66 to 70 percent of the new versions still bound. OpenAI says binding is only one step toward a useful medicine. Sources: OpenAI, AlphaSignal, StartupHub.ai.
