item.nf:article: {"headline":"OpenAI says GPT-6.2 designed proteins that bound their targets in lab tests","dek":"In work with the lab Onava, 35 of 322 small proteins built from GPT-6.2 designs bound their targets, though specialized tools still screened the candidates.","summary":"OpenAI said on November 24, 2026 that its GPT-6 models can design new protein shapes and sequences using reasoning and code alone. In lab tests, 35 of 322 minibinders based on GPT-6.2 designs bound their intended targets, with at least one hit for each of five targets.","seo_title":"OpenAI GPT-6.2 designs proteins that bind in lab tests","seo_description":"OpenAI says GPT-6.2 designed proteins with reasoning and code alone: 35 of 322 minibinders bound their targets in Onava's lab. The results and the limits.","answer_summary":"OpenAI reports that GPT-6.2 produced 3D protein designs and new sequences without calling specialized design models, and that 35 of 322 resulting minibinders bound their targets in the lab, but other specialized tools were still used to filter candidates.","tags":["OpenAI","GPT-6.2","Protein design","Biology","Research"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI said on November 24, 2026 that models in its GPT-6 family can design new protein shapes and the sequences of amino acids that make them up using only reasoning and code, without calling specialized biology models to generate the designs. The company described the work in a post and a preprint titled \"GPT-6 as a Universal Foundation Model for Protein Biology: Beyond Specialized Models.\"","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-models-demonstrate-intrinsic-protein-design-capabilities/"},{"name":"StartupHub.ai","url":"https://www.startuphub.ai/ai-news/ai-research/2026/gpt-6-designs-proteins-without-bio-models"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The lab experiments used a pre-release version of GPT-6.2, according to OpenAI. The proteins were produced and tested by Onava, a protein design company that worked with OpenAI on the project. AlphaSignal noted that the preprint has not been peer reviewed and that independent replication is still pending.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-models-demonstrate-intrinsic-protein-design-capabilities/"},{"name":"AlphaSignal","url":"https://alphasignal.ai/news/openai-s-gpt-6-2-designs-real-proteins-that-bind-drug-targets-in-the-lab"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the lab tests found","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In the first experiment, GPT-6.2 received 3D structures of five target proteins with the binding site marked, then wrote code to build 3D designs for minibinders, small proteins meant to attach to a target. A specialized model called SolubleMPNN suggested sequences for those shapes, and other specialized models filtered candidates. Of 322 minibinders tested, 35, or 10.9 percent, bound their intended target. The hits were spread across all five targets: 18 for IL-17A, 8 for VEGF-A, 5 for PD-L1, 3 for IL-7R alpha and 1 for TrkA.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-models-demonstrate-intrinsic-protein-design-capabilities/"},{"name":"AlphaSignal","url":"https://alphasignal.ai/news/openai-s-gpt-6-2-designs-real-proteins-that-bind-drug-targets-in-the-lab"},{"name":"StartupHub.ai","url":"https://www.startuphub.ai/ai-news/ai-research/2026/gpt-6-designs-proteins-without-bio-models"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A second test checked sequence design. GPT-6.2 was shown 3D models of known minibinders bound to their targets, without the original sequences, and asked to write new ones. For an MDM2 binder, 75 of 88 new sequences bound, or 85 percent. For VEGF-A the figure was 26 of 42, and for PD-1 it was 8 of 59. On three unpublished minibinder shapes, 14 of 107 proteins made from GPT-6.2 sequences bound. OpenAI said two of its sequences for one 90 amino acid PD-L1 binder differed from the original at more than half the positions, which it presented as evidence that the model was not simply recalling known answers.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-models-demonstrate-intrinsic-protein-design-capabilities/"},{"name":"StartupHub.ai","url":"https://www.startuphub.ai/ai-news/ai-research/2026/gpt-6-designs-proteins-without-bio-models"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The company also asked GPT-6.2 to redesign the three binding loops of antibodies. For six small VHH antibodies aimed at IL-4R alpha, 128 of 182 designs, about 70 percent, showed signs of binding. For five therapeutic antibodies that target PD-1 or PD-L1, the model changed about half the amino acids in each loop, and 179 of 272 fragments, about 66 percent, still bound the original target.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-models-demonstrate-intrinsic-protein-design-capabilities/"},{"name":"AlphaSignal","url":"https://alphasignal.ai/news/openai-s-gpt-6-2-designs-real-proteins-that-bind-drug-targets-in-the-lab"},{"name":"StartupHub.ai","url":"https://www.startuphub.ai/ai-news/ai-research/2026/gpt-6-designs-proteins-without-bio-models"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Benchmarks and weak spots","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI also reported computer benchmarks, many of them for an unreleased internal research model rather than GPT-6.2. On the MotifBench scaffolding test, that internal model produced passing designs 43.7 percent of the time, compared with 27.8 percent for the specialized tool RFdiffusion. In small molecule docking on the PoseBusters set, GPT-6.2 matched the experimental pose in 93 percent of scored cases, against 50 percent for DiffDock-L.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-models-demonstrate-intrinsic-protein-design-capabilities/"},{"name":"AlphaSignal","url":"https://alphasignal.ai/news/openai-s-gpt-6-2-designs-real-proteins-that-bind-drug-targets-in-the-lab"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The company listed clear limits. Predicting a full protein structure from its sequence remained a weak point: the internal model averaged a TM-score of 0.38, far below the 0.93 of the specialized predictor ESMFold2. OpenAI said the campaign still relied on specialized models such as Boltz-2 and ESMFold2 to filter candidates, so the results do not yet show end to end design without that help. It also said its 3D designs scored slightly lower than RFdiffusion in one comparison, and that hit rates depend heavily on how strictly designs are filtered before lab tests.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-models-demonstrate-intrinsic-protein-design-capabilities/"},{"name":"AlphaSignal","url":"https://alphasignal.ai/news/openai-s-gpt-6-2-designs-real-proteins-that-bind-drug-targets-in-the-lab"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI said binding is only one step toward a useful research tool or medicine, and that specificity, stability and biological activity would still need to be shown. The company also wrote that the same capabilities could be misused, and said it evaluates biosecurity risks under its Preparedness Framework.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-models-demonstrate-intrinsic-protein-design-capabilities/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The notable claim is less about any single protein and more about method. Protein design has relied on narrow tools trained for one job, and OpenAI is arguing that a general model can take over parts of that pipeline by reasoning through geometry and writing its own code. The lab numbers are a useful signal, but the strongest benchmark results come from a model the public cannot use, and the screening step still leaned on specialized software.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next test is outside review of the preprint and whether OpenAI or Onava show designed proteins doing something useful after they bind, which the company named as its next target.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Vercel v0 for free
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Sign in at v0.app, start a chat and describe what you want in plain words. A screenshot, a mockup or a Figma design also works as a starting point. Open the Design tab, select an element and change its style, then click Apply. Save your prompts for layout and behavior. Publish puts the app on a vercel.app address. Connect your own domain later. Reviews say the free plan has about $5 of credits a month. Sources: v0 docs: Quickstart, v0 docs: Introduction, v0 docs: FAQs, NxCode: v0 by Vercel complete guide 2026, Taskade: v0 by Vercel review 2026.

item.title: Claude can now turn the apps it builds into real Mac and Windows apps with one click
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Pick Install as app from an artifact's Share menu in Claude for Mac or Windows. The beta is rolling out on all plans. The app updates on its own when the artifact is edited. Apps can ask for notifications, menu bar items or full computer access to run programs and change files. Anthropic says it does not review apps before you install them. Sources: Anthropic, The Next Web, TestingCatalog.

TestingCatalog reports that the option also appears in the artifact's title menu and in a right-click menu, and that it requires desktop version 6.28899.0 or later, citing Anthropic's help center. There is no separate packaging or signing step and no API key, and users must be online and signed in to Claude to open an installed app.","sources":[{"name":"Anthropic","url":"https://claude.com/resources/articles/install-as-app"},{"name":"TestingCatalog","url":"https://www.testingcatalog.com/anthropic-now-allows-installing-artifacts-as-desktop-apps/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On a Mac, installed apps go into a Claude Apps folder inside the user's Applications folder, according to TestingCatalog, while on Windows they appear in the Start menu or as a desktop shortcut. The Next Web reports that the feature is not available on Linux, on the web or on mobile. Claude Docs, Slides and Sheets, legacy artifacts and live artifacts from Claude Cowork cannot be installed, TestingCatalog said.","sources":[{"name":"The Next Web","url":"https://thenextweb.com/news/claude-install-as-app-artifacts-mac-windows-desktop"},{"name":"TestingCatalog","url":"https://www.testingcatalog.com/anthropic-now-allows-installing-artifacts-as-desktop-apps/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"When the underlying artifact is edited, the installed app updates automatically. A permission covers only the current version of an app, so Claude asks again after every update, though parts of an app loaded from another website can change without a new request. The Next Web adds that zero data retention does not apply to these apps.","sources":[{"name":"Anthropic","url":"https://claude.com/resources/articles/install-as-app"},{"name":"The Next Web","url":"https://thenextweb.com/news/claude-install-as-app-artifacts-mac-windows-desktop"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic showed demo apps built by its staff, including a menu bar and tray app called Vitals for checking a computer's performance. item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Since November 24, servers built on MCP can ship skills to Claude and Claude Code: written guides for how to use their tools. Shopify, HubSpot and Atlassian are among the first. item.title: How to use Photoroom for product photos
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Upload a photo in the app or at app.photoroom.com. The background is removed automatically. Shoot on a plain surface in good light for the cleanest edge. Pick a plain white background for marketplaces, or let AI Backgrounds build a styled scene. Add an AI shadow so the product does not look pasted on. Batch mode applies the same edits to many photos at once. Free accounts get 250 exports a month. Paid plans start at $7.50 a month, billed yearly. Sources: Photoroom: Pricing, Photoroom: Batch mode, Photoroom: Background remover, eesel AI: Photoroom pricing guide.

item.title: Tidal will delete 27 million songs made entirely by AI
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Tidal said on November 24 that 43% of the tracks sent to it in the last 90 days were fully AI-generated. On November 6 alone, it was over 60%. From December 9, Tidal will reject and remove them. About 27 million tracks, 6.3% of Tidal's catalog, are tagged as fully AI. Tidal says 96% of them have no streams. Songs made with AI help can stay. Only tracks made entirely by AI go. Sources: TechCrunch, Mix, TIDAL Magazine.

item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Two or three sentences at most. Put your inclusion rules or PICO in Additional Context. Pick Keyword search for a formal review, Semantic search to explore. item.title: ChatGPT's paid users just got a new everyday model that can watch prices for you
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: OpenAI began rolling out a version of GPT-6.2 Sol tuned for everyday conversation on November 23, less than a week after it arrived in Work and Codex. It goes to Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise users first. In OpenAI's own tests, it scored 71.7% on image understanding, up from 47.4% for GPT-6. Comparing hotels, it can weigh a shorter walk against a lower rate, and it can offer to alert you when an item drops in price. OpenAI will retire GPT-5.6 Sol on December 23. GPT-5.6 Terra leaves Work and Codex the same day. Sources: 9to5Mac, Digital Trends, iGeeksBlog.

item.title: OpenAI and Cisco built a free AI shield that blocks attacks before Linux servers get patched
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Shirudo, Japanese for shield, runs small eBPF programs inside Linux that block a known exploit while the service keeps running. Teams can watch a shield in test mode first, then deploy it after approval, with no restart. In an OpenAI test, Codex built a shield that stopped a Java4Shell attack on a running Elasticsearch server. Shields are signed and checked before they load. The code is free on GitHub. Sources: OpenAI, SiliconANGLE, The Register.

The name is Japanese for shield, and the temporary protections it applies are called shields.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/"},{"name":"The Register","url":"https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/24/cisco-and-openai-pitch-ebpf-kernel-plugins-as-the-way-to-tame-the-patchpocalypse/5311795"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to OpenAI, the tool targets the gap between a disclosure and a fix. Shirudo lets operators check whether a shield stops the exploit behavior while legitimate requests still go through, then deploy it after approval without restarting the service.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How the shields work","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Shirudo is built on eBPF, a Linux technology that runs small programs at specific points inside the operating system to observe activity and apply targeted controls. The Register described these programs as sandboxed kernel plug-ins that do not get unrestricted access to system resources. OpenAI said operators can watch the effect of a proposed shield before switching it to enforcement.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/"},{"name":"The Register","url":"https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/24/cisco-and-openai-pitch-ebpf-kernel-plugins-as-the-way-to-tame-the-patchpocalypse/5311795"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI said shields are cryptographically signed and verified before they load, that the Linux eBPF verifier checks each program against safety rules, and that a Trusted Platform Module keeps a verifiable record of which protections were loaded or removed. The code is published on GitHub under the BSD 2-Clause license, with its BPF programs dual-licensed under BSD and GPL.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"SiliconANGLE reported that Shirudo is the first effort under what the two companies call the Secure Infrastructure Project, and that it grew out of Tetragon, an open-source runtime security project from Isovalent. The Register noted that Cisco owns Isovalent, which also created the Cilium networking project.","sources":[{"name":"SiliconANGLE","url":"https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/23/cisco-and-openai-launch-shirudo-an-open-source-infrastructure-shield-to-protect-against-ai-driven-cyberattacks/"},{"name":"The Register","url":"https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/24/cisco-and-openai-pitch-ebpf-kernel-plugins-as-the-way-to-tame-the-patchpocalypse/5311795"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"A Codex test against Java4Shell","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In a controlled test described by OpenAI, its Codex coding agent generated a shield that blocked an attempt to exploit Java4Shell, a recently disclosed Java flaw, against a running Elasticsearch service. OpenAI said the shield added an input check to Java's Base64 decoder and was attached to the live process, so the malicious input was rejected while Elasticsearch kept running.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/"},{"name":"SiliconANGLE","url":"https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/23/cisco-and-openai-launch-shirudo-an-open-source-infrastructure-shield-to-protect-against-ai-driven-cyberattacks/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"SiliconANGLE, citing Cisco, described a wider workflow in which Codex, given exploit details, builds a reproducer, designs a mitigation, validates it and deploys signed shields to every affected machine. OpenAI's own announcement describes these agent controls as something the companies are still designing, and The Register reported that the companies expect a human to check every shield before it reaches production.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/"},{"name":"SiliconANGLE","url":"https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/23/cisco-and-openai-launch-shirudo-an-open-source-infrastructure-shield-to-protect-against-ai-driven-cyberattacks/"},{"name":"The Register","url":"https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/24/cisco-and-openai-pitch-ebpf-kernel-plugins-as-the-way-to-tame-the-patchpocalypse/5311795"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Thomas Graf, Cisco's security chief technology officer, told SiliconANGLE that fixes can take weeks or even months, a delay he called no longer acceptable now that attackers often exploit flaws before fixes arrive. OpenAI President Greg Brockman said in the announcement that because so many teams rely on the same software, it makes sense to build these defenses in the open.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/"},{"name":"SiliconANGLE","url":"https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/23/cisco-and-openai-launch-shirudo-an-open-source-infrastructure-shield-to-protect-against-ai-driven-cyberattacks/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"A crowded patching problem","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Register placed the launch against a surge in vulnerability reports, saying more than 100,000 software flaws were reported this year, many after AI-powered bug finders appeared. It listed other companies that sell similar compensating controls, including VMware, Palo Alto Networks, Rapid7 and Rimini Street, and observed that the project is not entirely altruistic because it could raise demand for Codex.","sources":[{"name":"The Register","url":"https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/24/cisco-and-openai-pitch-ebpf-kernel-plugins-as-the-way-to-tame-the-patchpocalypse/5311795"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"In NeuraFeed's reading, Shirudo is an attempt to put AI on the defensive side of a race that AI bug hunting has sped up. The open license, signing and hardware-backed records address the trust question that comes with letting a model write code that runs inside the kernel. The published material so far shows one controlled demonstration, not results from large production fleets.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next signal is whether tested shields start shipping alongside vulnerability disclosures, a goal OpenAI named in its announcement, and whether Linux distributions or large cloud operators adopt the runtime. A technical deep dive for developers is scheduled for December 15, 2026.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Base44 to build a working app for free
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On the Base44 home screen, say who the app is for, what it helps them do and why it is useful. Keep the first prompt to the core idea. Add details later. Pick Plan in the mode menu beside Build. Base44 asks about your users, the main flows and the design. Plan messages cost a fraction of a credit. The first build costs about 1. Sources: Base44 Docs: Quick start guide, Base44 Docs: Starting from your first prompt, Base44 Docs: Prompt guide, Base44 Docs: Billing and plans, Base44 Pricing, TechCrunch, Wix Press Room.

Base44 is a fast way to get a real, working prototype; just do not expect a free app with your own domain, private access or payments.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: UC is giving 300,000 students ChatGPT for $1.2 million
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: UC signed a one-year, $1.2 million deal with OpenAI. ChatGPT Edu and the Codex coding agent go to students, staff and faculty starting December 1. The system has about 300,000 students and 265,000 workers. Cal State renewed its OpenAI deal in July: $39 million over three years for 470,000 students. UC's IT chief said UC "played hardball" and threatened to go with Anthropic instead. Sources: Sacramento Bee, EdSource via LAist, UC Office of the President.

nf:hero.nf:alt: A tablet screen showing the ChatGPT app icon next to icons of rival AI apps.

item.title: Anthropic now lets Claude approve code changes on its own, with no human click needed
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Claude Ship combines Code Review, which is already generally available, with two new beta agents: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. It works on GitHub repositories for Claude Team and Enterprise plans. PR Steward handles failing checks, merge conflicts and review feedback, then comments on what it changed and how to undo it. It cannot approve or merge code. Typing "@claude stop" halts it. Sources: TechCrunch, Digital Trends.

item.title: Claude claims a 47-year-old math proof no human has checked
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On November 23, Anthropic added a paper called "VP ≠ VNP over every field" to its public math repository, credited to an internal research version of Claude. It targets a question Leslie Valiant posed in 1979. The proof comes with Lean code that a computer can check. But the README says no human mathematician has checked the proof. It also says the result does not settle P vs NP. Sources: CASRAI, Kingy AI.

The material was added to a new vp-vnp directory in the company's public formal-math repository on GitHub on November 23, 2026, and the paper was also posted as a preprint.","sources":[{"name":"CASRAI","url":"https://casrai.org/news/anthropic-claude-authored-vp-vnp-proof-unverified-lean-2026"},{"name":"Kingy AI","url":"https://kingy.ai/blog/anthropic-claude-vp-vnp-proof/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Kingy AI reported that the paper credits an internal research version of Claude with the discovery, and that Anthropic researchers worked with the model to improve the presentation. VP contains families that can be computed by arithmetic circuits of polynomial size, built from addition and multiplication gates. VNP contains families that can be written as sums, over exponentially many zero and one assignments, of polynomials that are easy to compute. Leslie Valiant introduced the framework in a 1979 paper, \"Completeness classes in algebra,\" and showed that the permanent of a matrix is complete for VNP.","sources":[{"name":"CASRAI","url":"https://casrai.org/news/anthropic-claude-authored-vp-vnp-proof-unverified-lean-2026"},{"name":"Kingy AI","url":"https://kingy.ai/blog/anthropic-claude-vp-vnp-proof/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The permanent is computed like the determinant, but with every term added instead of some being subtracted. For a two by two matrix with entries a, b, c and d, the determinant is ad minus bc, while the permanent is ad plus bc, Kingy AI explained. The question of whether VP equals VNP asks, in effect, whether the permanent can be computed by small circuits.","sources":[{"name":"Kingy AI","url":"https://kingy.ai/blog/anthropic-claude-vp-vnp-proof/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to both reports, the paper claims that arithmetic circuits computing the permanent need superpolynomially many gates. In characteristic two, where the permanent and determinant coincide, the proof uses the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial instead. The stated lower bound is quasipolynomial, of the form m raised to c times the cube root of log m, for all sufficiently large m.","sources":[{"name":"CASRAI","url":"https://casrai.org/news/anthropic-claude-authored-vp-vnp-proof-unverified-lean-2026"},{"name":"Kingy AI","url":"https://kingy.ai/blog/anthropic-claude-vp-vnp-proof/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What has and has not been checked","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The release includes a Lean 4 formalization: a statement file that uses only the Mathlib library, and a larger body of Lean code that proves it. Kingy AI reported that the repository's automated check passed. CASRAI noted that the README lists additional tools, including an independently written proof kernel, for a fuller check.","sources":[{"name":"CASRAI","url":"https://casrai.org/news/anthropic-claude-authored-vp-vnp-proof-unverified-lean-2026"},{"name":"Kingy AI","url":"https://kingy.ai/blog/anthropic-claude-vp-vnp-proof/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The README, as quoted by CASRAI, says that both the paper and the formal code were written by AI models and that no human mathematician has checked the proof. It also warns that while Lean checks the proofs, no machine checks that the formal statement says what is claimed. The README states that the result does not settle P versus NP.","sources":[{"name":"CASRAI","url":"https://casrai.org/news/anthropic-claude-authored-vp-vnp-proof-unverified-lean-2026"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Kingy AI said it found no public, substantive verification by independent experts at the time of publication. CASRAI described the repository as a research artifact that is not maintained and does not accept contributions.","sources":[{"name":"CASRAI","url":"https://casrai.org/news/anthropic-claude-authored-vp-vnp-proof-unverified-lean-2026"},{"name":"Kingy AI","url":"https://kingy.ai/blog/anthropic-claude-vp-vnp-proof/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The release follows other recent mathematical claims linked to Anthropic, including an October 2026 paper on a fast algorithm for 3-SAT and a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis announced by Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge, CASRAI noted.","sources":[{"name":"CASRAI","url":"https://casrai.org/news/anthropic-claude-authored-vp-vnp-proof-unverified-lean-2026"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"A machine-checked proof removes much of the risk of a hidden logical error, but it does not remove the risk that the formal statement captures something weaker than the famous problem. That gap is exactly what the README flags, and it is why expert review of the Lean statement matters as much as the proof itself.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next signal is whether specialists in algebraic complexity confirm that the Lean statement matches Valiant's conjecture and whether the paper survives independent human review.","sources":[]}]}

Video in the Gemini app itself requires a Google AI plan.","seo_title":"How to use Veo for free in Google Flow (50 daily credits)","seo_description":"How to use Veo for free: open Google Flow, spend 50 daily credits on Veo 3.1 Lite clips, animate a photo with Frames, plus 4 prompts and the real limits.","answer_summary":"Open Google Flow at labs.google/fx/tools/flow in Chrome or Edge, sign in, and pick Veo 3.1 Lite. Every account gets 50 credits a day and each Lite clip costs 10, so you can make about five free clips daily.","tags":["Veo","Google Flow","Gemini","AI video","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"If you want to know how to use Veo for free, go to Google Flow, not the Gemini app. Flow gives every account without a subscription basic video generation and 50 credits a day, and a Veo 3.1 Lite clip costs 10 of them. That works out to five short clips a day at no cost.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353333"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: models","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: getting started","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16352836"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Gemini app changed this year. Google's help center says video in the app now uses Gemini Omni Flash, which replaced Veo 3.1 there, and the limits page lists video generation as unavailable without a Google AI plan. So the free path to Veo runs through Flow.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: create videos","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16126339"},{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: limits","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16275805"},{"name":"Engadget","url":"https://www.engadget.com/2176590/googles-gemini-omni-can-generate-anything-from-any-input-starting-with-video/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Before you start","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Flow requires you to be 18 or older, with your age verified through your Google account, and to live in a supported country. Google says to use a Chromium browser such as Chrome or Edge. Free users may find video generation unavailable at busy times, roughly 2 to 5 PM UTC.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353333"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: getting started","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16352836"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Veo for free in Flow, step by step","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open Flow and sign in","text":"Go to labs.google/fx/tools/flow in Chrome or Edge and sign in with your Google account. Your 50 daily credits refresh the day after your first generation, and unused credits do not carry over, so there is no point saving them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Choose Veo 3.1 Lite in the settings","text":"In the prompt box you can set the model, the aspect ratio, the number of outputs and the clip length. Pick Veo 3.1 Lite and a length of 4, 6 or 8 seconds. Lite clips are 720p. Keep the number of outputs at one if you want your credits to last.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Type a prompt and generate","text":"Describe one shot, not a whole film. Credits are taken when a generation starts and refunded within an hour if it fails or is blocked by a safety filter. If audio fails, Flow shows an Audio Generation Failed message and refunds those credits too. There is also a setting to return silent videos.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Animate your own photo with Frames","text":"Under Video, choose Frames, then add a start frame. You can also add an end frame and let the model fill the motion in between. Veo 3.1 Lite supports a first frame or a first and last frame.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Use Ingredients to keep a character","text":"Under Video, choose Ingredients and add images by dragging them in, typing @ and the asset name, or using Add and then Upload media. With Veo 3.1 Lite, ingredients only work for 8 second clips.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Flow's help center lists these costs: Veo 3.1 Lite is 10 credits per clip for everyone. Omni Flash 1.2 is also open to free users, for clips up to 10 seconds, at 1 credit per second at 360p or 3 per second at 720p. Veo 3.1 Fast, Veo 3.1 Quality and Omni Flash 1.1 are being retired on December 5, 2026.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353333"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: models","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Veo prompts to copy","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A product shot","text":"Slow orbit around a [product] on a wooden table by a window, soft morning light, shallow depth of field, steam rising from a coffee cup in the background.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A street scene with sound","text":"Handheld shot walking down a busy [city] street market at dusk, vendors calling out, string lights turning on, the camera stops at a fruit stall. Natural crowd sounds.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Bring a photo to life (use with Frames)","text":"The person in the photo slowly turns toward the camera and smiles, a light breeze moves their hair, the background stays still.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A simple explainer shot","text":"Top-down shot of hands drawing a [simple diagram] on white paper with a black marker, one line at a time, clean and well lit.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Five clips a day goes fast. Test a new idea with a 4 second clip first, then spend credits on an 8 second version once the shot looks right.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What free users do not get","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Extending clips, 15 second Omni clips and free upscaling to 1080p are for subscribers. Veo 3.1 Lite itself has no extend or video-to-video option. Paid plans add monthly Flow credits on top of the daily 50: 200 on Google AI Plus at $4.99 a month, 1,000 on AI Pro at $19.99, and 10,000 or 25,000 on AI Ultra, which starts at $99.99.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353333"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: models","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234"},{"name":"Google AI plans","url":"https://gemini.google/plans/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Every Flow video carries an invisible SynthID watermark. A visible watermark is an optional setting in the menu under your profile picture, except in India, South Korea and Vietnam, where it stays on for anyone below the top Ultra tier. Engadget also noted that SynthID is added to all Omni videos.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353333"},{"name":"Engadget","url":"https://www.engadget.com/2176590/googles-gemini-omni-can-generate-anything-from-any-input-starting-with-video/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"If you were hoping to use Veo for free through the Gemini API instead, Google's pricing page lists the Veo 3 and 3.1 free tier as not available. The API charges per second of video.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini API pricing","url":"https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Flow is the best free deal Google offers for AI video right now, but it is built around credits, and five Lite clips a day is enough to learn the tool, not to make a long project. Busy hours can block free users entirely. If you need longer clips, extensions or sharper output, that is where the paid plans start to make sense.","sources":[]}]}
